meta.title: The Bird in the Library
meta.textType: story: two versions of one event

paragraphs: On Thursday, a small bird flew into the school library during the club hour. Lily and Leo each wrote a post about it for the Explorers' Blog. Their two posts were a little different. Teacher Kim read both of them before they went online, because she reads every post first.

Posted by Lily. At the beginning of the club hour, a small yellow bird appeared at the library door. It flew over our table and sat on a lamp near the ceiling. Nobody moved, and the library was very quiet. "Where did it come from?" whispered Mia. "I do not know," said Teacher Kim. "Please stay still, and let us give it some time." Mia opened the big window, and we waited for ten minutes. Then the bird flew out and went up into a tree. Mia said, "It looks healthy, because it moves its wings well." We went back to our books, but we looked at the tree for a long time.

Posted by Leo. In the middle of the club hour, a small brown bird came through the door. I was drawing a cartoon, and I did not notice it at first. Then it flew up and sat on the ceiling lamp. I like running, but I stayed very still. "Is it lost?" asked May. "Do not touch it," said Teacher Kim. May opened the big window, and we waited for five minutes. Luckily, the bird found the window and flew away. It was a very exciting hour, and my cartoon is about it.

After the posts, Teacher Kim looked at the two posts and smiled. "Some facts are the same in both posts," she said. "The bird came on Thursday, and it flew out of the window." "Some details are different, because each writer saw the event from a different table." "Maybe the bird was yellow and brown." "Maybe ten minutes felt like five minutes." "Which post is right?" asked Leo. "Both are right for the writer," said Teacher Kim.

Teacher Kim filled in a form for the school nature board. She wrote the day, the place, and the name of the club. Then she gave every Explorer a small paper diploma. It said, "Bird Helper of the Library." Leo held his diploma over his head, and everybody laughed. "I will put both posts on the blog," said Lily. "People can read them and find the differences."
